result_on_the_question_batch_A_existed_t.question: Can a requirement statement keep its normative force without the standard's sentence?
result_on_the_question_batch_A_existed_t.answer: YES, and the modal distinction gets SHARPER when restated. The standard's sentence CARRIES the modal; it does not EXPLAIN it. aia-collecting-verifying-information now says outright that 6.4.7 is should and not shall because 19011 guides rather than requires - the reproduction never said that at all. aia-planned-changes-control now says the shall attaches to the MANNER of a change rather than its paperwork, which the original carried implicitly and a candidate could miss.
result_on_the_question_batch_A_existed_t.consequence: The policy stands for the remaining 91. 37 words to 6, ten for ten, none firing, none introduced.

cross_certification_contradiction.isms_f_says: auditor-objectivity :: the requirement that auditors do not audit their own work
cross_certification_contradiction.aims_ia_and_isms_ia_say: Neither ISO 19011 nor ISO/IEC 42001 [27001] forbids auditing work you contributed to - that rule is practice convention, and reading it as a requirement is the trap.
cross_certification_contradiction.why_it_matters: One certification teaches as a requirement the exact thing two others teach as NOT a requirement and specifically name as the trap. All three serve English from the same unauthenticated endpoint. A partner pulling get_concept across the catalogue - which is what an ISO practice does - finds us contradicting ourselves about what a standard says.
cross_certification_contradiction.my_reading_which_goes_through_the_instru: The auditor rows are right and ISMS-F is wrong. 27001 cl.9.2.2 asks for objectivity and impartiality; 'shall not audit their own work' is ISO/IEC 17021 language about CERTIFICATION BODIES, not internal audit.
required: Verify, with a positive control, then fix ISMS-F's auditor-objectivity row. This is a ONE-ROW EXCEPTION to ISMS-F being closed and it is worth reopening for - a contradiction is worse than either version.

Then sweep the class: any concept whose description asserts a requirement that another certification's description denies. Nothing currently performs that check and the corpus now spans four standards.

declared_citation_rows_has_stopped_worki.observation: All ten rows name a clause. The mechanism I set - you declare the citation rows, I read those in full - assumed citation rows were a minority. In AIMS-IA and ISMS-IA they are the population.
declared_citation_rows_has_stopped_worki.replacement: Each row reports the CLAIMS it makes and what verified each one, positive and negative alike.
declared_citation_rows_has_stopped_worki.negative_claims_need_a_positive_control: A negative claim cannot be verified by finding text, only by failing to find it, which is the vacuous-pass shape. You already did this right once: top-management's 'delegate is absent from 27001' was checked with a self-test proving the search would have found the phrase if it were there. That becomes the rule for every negative claim rather than a thing done on one row.
